This appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants aggrieved by inadequate compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.2846/2012 dated 17.07.2014 by the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Belgaum.

Belgaum
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The mother of the appellants/claimants died in road traffic accident.
The appellants/claimants being daughters, made a claim for compensation and the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,55,000/- with 6% interest.
The appellants/claimants being aggrieved by inadequate compensation awarded, they have filed this appeal.

3. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondent.
4.

The learned counsel for the appellants would contend that the accident has occurred in the year 2012 and the Tribunal has taken notional income of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11361 deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month, it ought to have taken Rs.6,500/- as per chart prepared by legal service authority for the purpose of Lok-Adalat.
He submits that the Tribunal has not awarded consortium but only awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of love and affection.
He contends that the appellants/claimants being daughters are entitled to consortium in a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-(40,000x3).
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses but it ought to have awarded Rs.30,000/- under the said head.
On these grounds, he prayed to allow the appeal.
5. The learned counsel for the respondent would contend that the Tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased and compensation awarded is just and proper.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsels, the Court has perused the impugned judgment and trial Court records.
The deceased was aged about 67 years as on the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11361 date of accident.
The accident occurred in the year 2012.
As per the chart prepared for settlement of the cases before Lok-Adalat by the legal service authority, notional income for the year 2012 has to be taken at Rs.6,500/- per month.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.6,500/- as against Rs.3,000/-.

Therefore, the appellants are entitled to compensation for loss of dependency would be:
6500 x 12 x 5 x 2/3 =2,60,000/-
7.
The appellants being daughters of the deceased, they are entitled for consortium in a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-(40,000x3).
The appellants/petitioners are also entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses and loss of estate as against Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In view of the above, the appellants are entitled to compensation of Rs.4,10,000/- as against Rs.1,50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11361 appellants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,60,000/- with interest.

9. In the result, the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part with cost.
ii. The appellants are entitled to  enhanced compensation of Rs.2,60,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

iii. The respondent is directed to deposit  the enhanced compensation with interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. The entire enhanced compensation shall be release to the appellants.
Sd/-
(SHIVASHANKAR AMARANNAVAR) JUDGE RKM, CT:ANB Annavva Bhairappa Badiger vs The Divisional Controller on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10092056/
